_note: ALERTS, THE FIREWALL, AND THE CUES THAT WERE MISSING. Mike, 2026-09-12: 'other improvement
sounds we need like alerts, when the firewall comes and more'.
⚠ THE POINT OF AN ALERT IS THAT IT FIRES ONCE AND MEANS SOMETHING. Mike has complained about
beeping three separate times - the jet flyby (0807q), the missile lock-on (0813A) and 'beep
beep beep with all these bosses' (0822ae, which was enemyShoot firing per BULLET). In every
case the fault was REPETITION, not the sample. These are written to be heard once, at a moment
that matters, and they are wired with a cooldown.
So none of these is a beep. An alert that repeats becomes noise however good it sounds.

sounds.prompt: A heavy warning klaxon for an approaching capital ship. One deep rising horn blast with a metallic edge and a low rumble underneath, ominous and final. Starts immediately at full weight. Dry, no music, no reverb tail. Retro arcade video game boss warning.
A single urgent alarm blip, bright and hard edged, one short rising electronic tone with a sharp attack. Clean and immediate. Dry, no reverb, no music, no repeat. Retro arcade video game warning.

A targeting system acquiring a lock. A fast tightening electronic sweep that snaps into one solid confirming tone, mechanical and cold. Sharp and short. Dry, no reverb, no music. Retro arcade video game missile lock.

A huge weapon charging to fire. A rising electrical whine building in pitch and intensity with crackling energy, tense and threatening, ending right as it peaks. Dry, no reverb, no music. Retro arcade video game charge up.

A towering wall of fire erupting across the screen. A deep igniting WHOOMPH at the very start then a sustained roaring blaze with crackling embers, huge and dangerous. The ignition is the loudest moment. Dry and close, no reverb tail, no music. Retro arcade video game firewall hazard.
A sheet of flame sweeping past and dying down. A rushing airy whoosh with a fading crackle, receding fast. Dry, no reverb, no music. Retro arcade video game flame sweep.

A short two-note electronic warning chirp, bright and clipped, the sound a cabinet makes right before something dangerous happens. Sharp attack, no tail. Dry, no reverb, no music. Retro arcade video game telegraph cue.

A heavy armoured barrier absorbing a hit and refusing it. A dull metallic clang immediately followed by a low denying synthetic thrum, solid and unbreakable. Dry, no reverb, no music. Retro arcade video game blocked hit.
